citations.name: habeas:coverage
citations.commentary:
TermLike requires this callback on the unit-test-only adapter.
 The fixed-width display tests request no horizontal cursor movement,
 so this no-op has no application behavior to test. Real terminal
 movement remains exercised through the PTY integration test.

rationale:
The `habeas:coverage` citation on `src/execution_coverage/progress.rs#mod[tests]/impl[RecordingTerm/indicatif::TermLike]/fn[move_cursor_left]` meets the built-in's criteria.

- **Form:** It is a fenced `{cite}` on an explicit function with a body. The commentary is part of the assessed item text.
- **Substance:** The explanation gives reasons beyond difficulty:
  - `TermLike` requires the callback.
  - The adapter exists only in the unit-test module.
  - The method is a no-op returning `Ok(())`, so it has no application behavior to test.
- **Agreement with the source:**
  - `move_cursor_left` returns `Ok(())` and does nothing.
  - A search of `src/execution_coverage/progress.rs` finds no call to it. The unit tests that use `RecordingTerm` (`stage_and_conversion_counts_are_visible_then_cleared` and `preparation_activity_keeps_updating_without_a_stage_change`) never request horizontal movement.
  - The PTY integration test the commentary relies on exists. It is `coverage_progress_on_a_pty_preserves_reports_and_plain_output_policy` in `tests/execution_coverage.rs`, which runs the real binary on a pseudo-terminal and asserts that progress updates in place. This supports the claim that real terminal behavior is exercised there.

No gap found.
